Artifact-identity hold: the encoded-observation-representation identity strategy cannot distinguish repeated projections of the same record version by different agents, the result-payload-object identity contradicts the model's own rule that a locator or file name is never an identifier, and the original-acquisition-record is many-to-one against the observations that claim it. These three defects must be corrected or explicitly disclosed in the published draft.

Entry-kind hold: the frozen registry carries entry_kind standalone-mm, which classifies the record plane only. Publication must state the subject-model kind as event alongside the record-plane value, so that no consumer treats standalone-mm as a semantic classification of the observation itself.
Independent second-provider review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this Claude-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Obtain and read the published OGC 20-082r4 / ISO 19156:2023 requirements classes directly, then re-derive every required element and multiplicity in this model against them and retire the 2021 draft feature catalogue as the cardinality basis.

Split the composite source identifiers into one id per publication (JCGM 100, 101, 102, 106, 200, GUM-1, GUM-6; ILAC-G8 and ILAC-G17 separately), obtain parseable texts of GUM and VIM, and re-attach clause-level citations to the uncertainty, measurand and traceability findings.

Design an uncertainty, traceability and conformity function for the next revision so that the whole layer is reachable through the function set, together with functions for identifier resolution and duplicate reconciliation, provenance and derivation binding, and access classification, embargo and hold registration.

Verify WMO-No. 1192 WIGOS Metadata Standard and the QARTOD flag manual from their publications rather than a wiki page and a programme landing page, and re-assess the findings that currently lean on SRC-015 and SRC-016 as one of only three or four refs.

Refer the registry placement to the Dimension Registrar: NAV.PHY.MAT.OBS, the PHY.MAT.OBS domain tags, the WM-MAT identifier prefix and the 0.00 robotics factor all understate a model whose evidence spans geospatial, clinical, oceanographic and meteorological practice and whose SOSA grounding is sensor-centric.

Resolve whether measurement uncertainty is taken into account in the conformity decision (guard-band treatment under ILAC-G8) needs its own question, since the current interp-decision-rule and interp-risk-basis pair records the rule and the accepted risk but not how uncertainty entered the judgement.

Populate the relationship contract with the eleven asserted neighbours, assigning link types and stating which side owns each referent, so the ownership boundary becomes machine-checkable rather than prose.

model.name: Invoice / Commercial Document
model.purpose: Provide one format-neutral context structure for commercial billing documents (invoice, credit note, debit note, self-billed invoice and their corrections) so an agent can understand, create, validate, exchange, prove and retain them across jurisdictions and syntaxes.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the commercial billing document as an aggregate: its identity and type, the parties and commercial content it asserts, its tax and monetary computation, the documents it references, its lifecycle and authenticity, and the exchange, retention and governance controls that make it legally usable. It is deliberately narrower than the legacy N1 'Document & Record' entry: generic recordkeeping mechanics are delegated to the record model, and the financial consequences of the document (payment, posting, tax return) are delegated to sibling models. Storage format and access interface are projections: UBL XML, UN/CEFACT CII, hybrid PDF/A-3, JSON, Markdown, Git, MCP or MongoDB carry the same semantics.
in_scope: Billing document family and function: invoice, credit note, debit note, self-billed invoice and self-billed credit note, corrective and cancelling documents, simplified invoices, summary/periodic invoices, proforma invoices, and the document-type and profile codes that distinguish them.
Document identity and numbering, including issuer-scoped sequential numbers and tax-authority clearance identifiers where a clearance regime applies.
Party roles carried on the document (seller, buyer, payee, seller tax representative, deliver-to party) as references to externally governed party records.
Commercial content: invoice lines, item identification and classification, quantities and unit codes, prices, document- and line-level allowances and charges, invoicing period.
Tax treatment and monetary computation: tax category and rate breakdown, exemption reasons, reverse charge, document and tax-accounting currency, totals, rounding and arithmetic consistency.
Payment instruction data carried on the document: payment means, terms, due date, payee account and remittance reference (not the payment event itself).
References to order, contract, despatch advice, receiving advice, tender/lot, project, preceding invoices and supporting attachments.
Lifecycle and status of the document, buyer response, dispute, correction and cancellation.
Authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility: business controls and reliable audit trail, electronic signature or seal, cryptographic fixity, tax-authority clearance and registration.
Regulatory conformance evidence: mandatory particulars, national usage specifications, validation results against schema and business rules.
Exchange semantics: syntax binding and semantic fidelity, routing identifiers, envelope and delivery evidence.
Retention, storage, legibility over the storage period, legal holds and disposition, including the tension with personal-data erasure.
Ownership, role-scoped access projections and provenance/audit trail.
out_of_scope: Payment execution, settlement, clearing, reconciliation state and remittance advice processing (delegated to WM-ECO-009 Payment / Settlement).
Order placement, contract formation and negotiation of commercial terms (delegated to the order and contract models).
Physical or digital fulfilment, despatch and goods receipt events (delegated to WM-ECO-024 Order Fulfilment).
Accounting postings, journal entries, revenue recognition and general-ledger treatment.
Periodic tax returns, digital reporting submissions (DRR), SAF-T extracts and audit-file generation; only the invoice-side data they draw on is modelled here.
Party master data and legal-entity registration; the model references party identifiers rather than governing them.
Product and service master data, catalogues and price lists.
Receivables financing, factoring, assignment, dunning and collections.
Point-of-sale fiscal receipts and cash-register fiscalisation devices.
Generic recordkeeping mechanics (rendition management, custody transfer, disposition machinery) beyond invoice-specific obligations; these belong to the document-and-record model.
Operation of exchange networks (service metadata publishing, transport certificates, access-point onboarding).

boundary_notes.distinction: The invoice carries a payment instruction (means, terms, due date, amount due) as an assertion at issue time; it does not carry settlement state. Whether the invoice was paid, partially paid or written off is derived by reference to settlement records, never stored as a mutable field on an issued document.

Despatch advice and receiving advice identifiers appear on the invoice as references supporting three-way matching, and the actual delivery date is a tax-relevant business term on the invoice; the fulfilment events themselves and their exceptions are governed by the fulfilment model.

This model narrows the legacy generic record entry. Version chains, renditions, custody transfer and disposition machinery are reused from the record model; what is specific here is that an issued invoice is immutable and is corrected by a new document rather than by a new version, so the generic version-chain pattern must not be applied to invoice content.

The invoice supplies data to periodic returns and to transaction-level digital reporting, and under clearance regimes the reporting act can precede delivery to the buyer; but the report is a separate governed submission with its own identity, deadline and correction rules and is not a projection of this model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Exchange network (Peppol eDelivery and comparable four-corner frameworks)
boundary_notes.distinction: Participant identifiers, service metadata lookup, transport profile and envelope are referenced so that routing and delivery evidence can be attached, but network operation and transport-level acknowledgement are outside the document. Transport receipt is not business acceptance.

The invoice references a purchase order, contract and tender/lot; it does not restate contractual terms. Where invoice terms contradict contract terms, the model records the discrepancy as a dispute input rather than resolving it.

Tax amounts and totals on the invoice are the legally asserted figures; the accounting entries derived from them (including any different functional-currency amounts) belong to the ledger model and may legitimately differ in presentation without invalidating the document.

sources.title: Universal Business Language Version 2.1
sources.organization: OASIS Universal Business Language Technical Committee
sources.relevance: Defines the Invoice, CreditNote, DebitNote, SelfBilledInvoice and SelfBilledCreditNote document types and the common library (Party, Item, Price, TaxTotal, LegalMonetaryTotal, AllowanceCharge, DocumentReference) that is the dominant invoice syntax binding.

sources.title: Universal Business Language Version 2.4
sources.organization: OASIS Universal Business Language Technical Committee
sources.relevance: Current UBL major-library release; documents backward-compatibility policy across minor revisions, the ID/schemeID identifier pattern, the manifest-values principle (receivers may not infer omitted values), and invoice-adjacent document types including FreightInvoice, Reminder and RemittanceAdvice.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
sources.relevance: A registered Core Invoice Usage Specification of EN 16931 bound to UBL; supplies the billing profile identifier, customization identifier, supported document types, additional Peppol business rules layered on the CEN rules, and code-list bindings.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 — UBL Invoice syntax tree
sources.relevance: Element-by-element binding of EN 16931 business terms and groups (BT-1 invoice number, BT-2 issue date, BT-3 type code, BT-5/BT-6 currencies, BT-7 tax point date, BT-9 due date, BT-10 buyer reference, BT-13 order reference, BT-25 preceding invoice reference, BT-72 delivery date, BT-112/BT-115 totals, BG-4 seller, BG-7 buyer, BG-23 VAT breakdown, BG-25 invoice line) to UBL syntax.

sources.title: Registry of supporting artefacts to implement EN 16931
sources.version_or_date: Accessed August 2026; Schematron validation artefacts v1.3.16, EAS code list v16.0, VATEX code list v8.0, biannual spring/autumn release cycle
sources.relevance: Normative registry of validation artefacts, code lists (ISO 4217 currency, ISO 3166 country, UNTDID 1001/4461/5305/7143, UNECE unit codes, EAS, ICD, VATEX) and registered CIUS/Extensions used to implement the European invoice semantic model.

sources.title: VAT — Invoicing rules
sources.organization: European Commission — Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union
sources.relevance: States when invoices must be issued, the content of full and simplified invoices, the equivalence of electronic and paper invoices, issuance subject to recipient acceptance, and the flexibility of storage location and method.

sources.title: VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA)
sources.organization: European Commission — Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union
sources.version_or_date: Council Directive (EU) 2025/516, Regulation (EU) 2025/517, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/518; in force 14 April 2025
sources.relevance: Establishes the move to structured e-invoicing and transaction-level digital reporting, the removal of the recipient-acceptance precondition for domestic mandates from entry into force, and the staged timeline to 1 July 2030 and convergence by 1 January 2035.

sources.title: Directive 2014/55/EU on electronic invoicing in public procurement
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union (via EUR-Lex)
sources.relevance: Defines electronic invoice, core elements and syntax; mandates a European semantic standard; enumerates the core element set (process and invoice identifiers, invoice period, seller/buyer/payee, tax representative, contract reference, delivery details, payment instructions, allowance or charge information, line item information, totals, VAT breakdown) and the obligation on contracting authorities to receive and process compliant invoices.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile: full date-time with seconds, mandatory Z or numeric offset, leap-second handling, and the -00:00 convention for known UTC with unknown local offset.

sources.title: Council Directive 2006/112/EC on the common system of value added tax
sources.organization: Council of the European Union (via EUR-Lex)
sources.relevance: Title XI Chapter 3 is the legal source for the invoice as an instrument: definition of electronic invoice, documents treated as invoices and amending documents, obligation and time limit to issue, the exhaustive list of required invoice particulars including the sequential number, currency rules, recipient acceptance, authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility, and storage obligations.

sources.title: Explanatory notes on VAT invoicing rules (Council Directive 2010/45/EU)
sources.organization: European Commission — Directorate-General for Taxation and Customs Union
sources.relevance: Interprets authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility: any business controls creating a reliable audit trail between invoice and supply are acceptable, with advanced electronic signature and EDI as examples rather than requirements, and legibility must persist throughout the storage period. Explicitly informal and not legally binding.

sources.title: Peppol eDelivery Network specifications
sources.version_or_date: Specification index updated 2026-07-15; AS4 Transport Profile v2.0.3 (2024-04-22), SMP v1.4.0 and SML v1.3.0 (effective 2025-11-01), Business Message Envelope (SBDH) v2.0.2 (effective 2026-07-02), Identifier Usage Policy v4.4.0
sources.relevance: Supplies the four-corner exchange semantics referenced by this model: participant, document-type and process identifiers, service metadata lookup, transport profile, message envelope and message-level status — the boundary between transport receipt and business acceptance.

sources.title: Factur-X / ZUGFeRD hybrid electronic invoice specification
sources.organization: FNFE-MPE (Forum National de la Facture Électronique) with FeRD
sources.version_or_date: Factur-X 1.09.2 / ZUGFeRD 2.5.2, released 4 August 2026; CII syntax D22B
sources.relevance: Defines the hybrid PDF/A-3 plus embedded UN/CEFACT CII invoice and its profiles (MINIMUM, BASIC WL, BASIC, EN 16931, EXTENDED); the canonical case where one invoice has both a human-readable and a machine-readable carrier and their relationship must be governed.

sources.title: Nationwide E-Invoicing Framework (InvoiceNow)
sources.relevance: Evidence that the four-corner exchange framework and its access-point/solution-provider roles are adopted by authorities outside the EU, supporting the regional-generalisation claims and the separation of network role from document semantics.

sources.title: Universal Business Language Version 2.4
sources.relevance: Published by the OASIS Universal Business Language TC; defines the Invoice, CreditNote, DebitNote, SelfBilledInvoice, SelfBilledCreditNote and FreightInvoice document families, the Invoice as a request for payment from the Supplier Accounting Party to the Customer Accounting Party, InvoiceLine and Item structures, and the exclusion of tax-reporting documents.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
sources.relevance: Published by the OpenPeppol Post-Award Coordinating Community; supplies the CIUS of EN 16931:2017, party roles (Customer/Supplier, Creditor/Debtor), billing profiles P1-P9, credit and correction processes, calculation rules including BR-CO-16, and payment means scope.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL Invoice syntax
sources.relevance: Binds the semantic model to UBL Invoice elements: CustomizationID and ProfileID defaults, cbc:ID without scheme attribute, buyer reference versus purchase order reference, allowances and charges, InvoicePeriod, tax point date, LegalMonetaryTotal and amount formatting rules.

sources.title: EN 16931 compliance
sources.version_or_date: Page updated 5 March 2026; standard EN 16931-1 semantic CORE and CIUS rules
sources.relevance: European Commission Digital Building Blocks / eInvoicing page defining compliance at document, implementation and specification level, the CORE model, and the rule that a CIUS must be a subset of CORE and must not break CORE rules.

sources.title: Council Directive 2006/112/EC Article 226 - Content of invoices
sources.version_or_date: Directive of 28 November 2006; Article 226 content of invoices
sources.relevance: Official text of the VAT Directive as published on legislation.gov.uk; sets the mandatory invoice content model: sequential number based on one or more series, party names, addresses and VAT identification numbers, supply date, quantity and nature of supply, unit price exclusive of VAT, discounts, taxable amount per rate, VAT rate and amount, exemption or reverse-charge references, and the 'Self-billing' and 'Cash accounting' mentions.

sources.title: 19 CFR 141.86 Contents of invoices and general requirements
sources.version_or_date: Current 19 CFR 141.86 (origin T.D. 73-175; last cited amendment CBP Dec. 09-47)
sources.relevance: Legal Information Institute reproduction of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection regulation prescribing commercial invoice contents for import entry: port of entry; time, place and parties to the sale or shipment; merchandise description, marks and package numbers; quantities; purchase price or alternative value; kind of currency; itemized charges; rebates and bounties; country of origin; assists; English-language requirement; packing list; and the named responsible exporter employee.

sources.title: UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice (CII) and Cross Industry Invoicing Process BRS
sources.version_or_date: CII maximum dataset; BRS Cross Industry Invoice v2.00.05; Executive Guide on eInvoicing 2023
sources.relevance: UNECE UN/CEFACT entry point describing CII as a maximum dataset covering commercial, transport, customs, fiscal and banking uses, and the acknowledged CII syntax binding for EN 16931.

sources.title: BRS Cross Industry Invoice v2.0.5
sources.version_or_date: Version 2.00.05, TBG approval 12 November 2008; PDF still published by UNECE
sources.relevance: UN/CEFACT TBG1 business requirements specification for the cross industry invoicing process, including supplier-initiated invoicing, self-billing with supplier reconciliation and dispute notice, self-billing credit notes, and consolidated, consignment and factored invoice variants; source of UNTDID 1001 document type usage.

bundles.name: Document identity, typing and issuance authority
bundles.description: What this document is, how it is uniquely and lawfully named, which functional class it belongs to, which specification it claims to follow, and who was entitled to issue it when.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream operation — matching, correction, clearance, retention, dispute — resolves on document identity and type. Identity is contested in practice because a clearance regime may mint an identifier that outranks the issuer's own number, so it must be settled first.

layers.name: Identity, type and specification claim
layers.description: The identifiers, functional type codes and specification/profile claims that make a billing document addressable and interpretable.

findings.name: Invoice identity and number scoping
findings.description: An invoice is identified by a number that is unique within the issuer's namespace and, in EU law, drawn from a sequential series; the number alone is not globally unique, so identity is the pair (issuer party identifier, invoice number) qualified by document type. Where a clearance regime applies, a second, authority-assigned identifier exists and legally outranks the issuer's number.

questions.text: Within which issuer namespace and document-type scope is this invoice number guaranteed unique, and what qualifies it to global uniqueness?
answer_data: Issuer party identifier with its scheme (ISO 6523 ICD or EAS)
Document type code used as part of the uniqueness scope
Statement of the uniqueness guarantee and its enforcing system

questions.text: Which system of record assigned this identifier, and does an authority-assigned clearance identifier exist that takes precedence?
answer_data: Assigning system identifier and its role (issuer ERP, service provider, tax authority)
Clearance identifier value and scheme where applicable
Precedence declaration naming the authoritative identifier
Evidence link to the assignment response

questions.text: What sequence rule governs the number series, and how are gaps, resets and per-establishment series explained?
answer_data: Series prefix or key and reset policy
Sequence rule statement (strictly sequential, per-year, per-establishment)
Jurisdictional basis for the sequence requirement

questions.text: Which internal surrogate keys exist for this document and how are they prevented from being presented as the legal invoice number?
answer_data: Surrogate key values and their type (UUID, ULID)
Projection rule marking surrogates as non-legal
Systems permitted to emit each key

data_elements.name: Invoice number
data_elements.description: The issuer-assigned identifier of the document, unique within the issuer's series.

data_elements.name: Issuer party identifier
data_elements.description: Registered identifier of the issuing party, with the scheme that governs it, used to scope the invoice number.

data_elements.name: Authoritative document identifier
data_elements.description: The identifier declared authoritative for this document, naming the assigning system and precedence basis.

data_elements.name: Internal surrogate key
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension for internal correlation only.

data_elements.name: Number series rule
data_elements.description: Declaration of the sequence rule, reset policy and gap-explanation obligation for the number series.

artifacts.name: Identity binding record
artifacts.description: A durable record binding the issuer party identifier, invoice number, document type, any clearance identifier and internal surrogates, with the precedence declaration and the assignment evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the declared authoritative identifier; issuer number plus issuer party identifier used as fallback when no clearance identifier exists.

findings.name: Document type, function and family membership
findings.description: The functional class of the document — commercial invoice, credit note, debit note, self-billed invoice, corrected invoice, proforma — expressed as a governed type code, plus its function (original, copy, duplicate). Type determines which rules apply, whether a preceding-document reference is mandatory, and whether the amounts are claims or reversals.

questions.text: Which governed type code classifies this document, and from which code list version is it drawn?
answer_data: Code list identifier and version (UNTDID 1001 as constrained by the profile)
Restriction applied by the profile or usage specification

questions.text: What obligations does this document type trigger that other types in the family do not?
answer_data: Rule identifiers that fire only for this type

questions.text: Is this document a legal invoice or a non-fiscal instrument such as a proforma or request for payment, and what marks the distinction?
answer_data: Type code and any national qualifier
Statement of whether tax becomes accountable on this document
Downstream systems permitted to consume it

questions.text: Is this instance an original, a copy or a duplicate, and how is that status carried across syntaxes?
answer_data: Relationship to the original instance identifier

data_elements.name: Document type code
data_elements.description: Governed code classifying the functional type of the billing document.

data_elements.name: Family role
data_elements.description: Whether the document asserts a claim, a reversal, an adjustment or a non-fiscal request.

data_elements.name: Copy indicator
data_elements.description: Marks the instance as original, copy or duplicate.

data_elements.name: Fiscal status
data_elements.description: Declares whether the document has legal invoice effect in the governing jurisdiction.

artifacts.name: Document type code mapping table
artifacts.description: Mapping between the governed type code, the family role, the type-conditional rule set and the equivalent codes in each supported syntax and national specification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by code list identifier plus version plus code value.

findings.name: Specification identifier, profile and conformance claim
findings.description: An invoice instance declares which semantic specification and which business process it follows, typically as a customization identifier plus a profile identifier. A usage specification may restrict the core model, and an extension may add to it; the claim determines which validation artefacts apply and what a receiver may assume.

questions.text: Which specification identifier and process profile identifier does this instance declare?
answer_data: Base semantic standard named by the claim
Release or version of the usage specification

questions.text: Does the declared specification restrict, extend or exactly implement the core semantic model, and which elements are affected?
answer_data: Extension list (elements added beyond the core)
Registry entry for the usage specification
Statement of whether core semantics are preserved

questions.text: What evidence supports the conformance claim, rather than the claim being asserted without proof?
answer_data: Validation artefact identifier and version applied
Validation outcome with timestamp and executing actor

questions.text: How does a receiver signal which specifications it can accept, and what happens when the declared profile is unsupported?
answer_data: Receiver capability declaration and its lookup mechanism

data_elements.name: Customization identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the semantic specification and usage rules the instance claims to follow.

data_elements.name: Profile identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the business process the document participates in.

data_elements.name: Specification relationship
data_elements.description: Whether the declared specification is a plain implementation, a restricting usage specification or an extension.

data_elements.name: Validation artefact version
data_elements.description: Version of the validation artefact set associated with the declared specification.

artifacts.name: Conformance claim record
artifacts.description: Record binding the declared customization and profile identifiers to the registry entry, the applicable validation artefact version and the evidence of the last successful validation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by customization identifier plus artefact version; linked to the document's authoritative identifier.

layers.name: Issuance context and authority
layers.description: When the document was issued relative to the supply, which dates carry legal weight, and who was entitled to issue it.

findings.name: Issue date, tax point and invoicing period
findings.description: An invoice carries several distinct dates with different legal effect: the issue date, the tax point date on which tax becomes accountable, the actual delivery date and the invoicing period for periodic billing. These are calendar dates in the core semantic model, not instants, which creates a real tension with instant-valued system timestamps.

questions.text: Which distinct dates does this document carry, and what legal effect does each one have?
answer_data: Tax point date value where it differs from the issue date
Actual delivery or supply completion date
Invoicing period start and end for periodic billing

questions.text: Was the document issued within the statutory time limit measured from the chargeable event, and how is that assessed?
answer_data: Applicable statutory deadline rule and jurisdiction
Justification where the deadline was missed

questions.text: Which time zone and calendar govern a date-only business term, and how is it reconciled with instant-valued system timestamps?
answer_data: Governing time zone or jurisdiction for date interpretation
Corresponding system instant with explicit offset
Rule preventing silent widening of a date into a timestamp

questions.text: How are the asserted business dates distinguished from the times at which the document was received, validated and archived?
answer_data: Event time values asserted by the issuer
Observation or ingestion instants recorded by each handling system
Divergence flag where business and observation times are inconsistent

findings.description: The party legally obliged to issue an invoice is not always the party that produces it. Issuance may be outsourced to a service provider or performed by the customer under a self-billing arrangement; in either case the supplier remains responsible, and the arrangement must be evidenced.

bundles.name: Parties and commercial content
bundles.description: Who the document is between and what it actually bills for: party roles and their identifiers, invoice lines, item identification, quantities, prices, allowances and charges.
bundles.rationale: The core semantic model of an electronic invoice is explicitly built from seller, buyer, payee and tax-representative information plus line item, allowance/charge and delivery information; these are the assertions that carry commercial and evidential weight.

layers.name: Party roles and identification

findings.name: Party roles, identifiers, addresses and establishment
findings.description: A billing document distinguishes seller, buyer, payee, seller tax representative and deliver-to party. Addresses matter because place of supply and establishment affect tax treatment.

findings.description: An invoice line groups a billed quantity, a unit of measure, a net amount, a tax category assignment and optional line-level period and references. Lines are the unit at which matching, dispute and partial credit operate, so line identity must be stable and referenceable from other documents.

findings.description: Pricing on a billing document separates the item net price, an optional gross price and price discount, a base quantity, and separately itemised allowances and charges at both line and document level, each with a reason and a reason code. Allowances and charges carry their own tax category, so they are not simple arithmetic adjustments.

Where a jurisdiction requires evidence of the rate used, that evidence is captured as a supporting attachment under the attachments finding rather than duplicated here.

The chain of such documents, not a version history, is the true history of the commercial claim.

findings.name: Lifecycle states, transitions and immutability point
findings.description: A billing document passes through preparation, issue, transmission, delivery, receipt, acceptance or rejection, correction and archiving. The decisive property is that content becomes immutable at issue: subsequent change is achieved by a new document, not by editing. Under clearance regimes an authority step is inserted before the document may lawfully be delivered.

data_elements.name: Response instant

data_elements.name: Dispute state
data_elements.description: Whether the document is under dispute and the scope of that dispute.

artifacts.description: A returned message carrying the response kind, coded reasons, affected elements and the responding party, distinct from any transport-level acknowledgement.

findings.name: Self-billing, prepayment and special processes
findings.description: UN/CEFACT CII treats traditional supplier-initiated invoices and self-billing as first-class processes; the customer raises a self-billing invoice and the supplier reconciles it, raising a dispute notice on discrepancy, corrected by a self-billing credit note. UBL SelfBilledInvoice is created by the Customer Accounting Party. Article 226(10a) requires the mention 'Self-billing'. Prepayment invoices (386) collect amounts to be subtracted from a final invoice. CII also names consolidated, consignment and factored variants. These are rare relative to 380 but are not optional footnotes in a full model.

questions.text: Is this a self-billed invoice, which agreement authorises it, and has the supplier accepted or disputed it?
If this is a prepayment invoice, which final invoice will absorb the prepaid amount, or if this is a final invoice, which prepayments are deducted?
Is the invoice consolidated, consignment (non-sale), factored or freight-charge billing, and which process rules then apply?

data_elements.name: prepaymentFlag

data_elements.name: consolidatedFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance is a consolidated invoice variant named by UN/CEFACT CII.

data_elements.name: consignmentFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance is a consignment (non-sale) invoice variant, UNCL 1001 code 395.

data_elements.name: disputeNoticeId

artifacts.name: Self-billed invoice

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the sequential number assigned by the issuing customer under the self-billing agreement, bound to the supplier party whose supply it documents.

layers.name: Authenticity, integrity and authority clearance
layers.description: The controls and authority acts that make the document trustworthy as evidence.

findings.name: Authenticity of origin, integrity of content and business controls
findings.description: Authenticity of origin and integrity of content must be assured from issue to the end of the storage period. The law is technology-neutral: any business controls creating a reliable audit trail between the invoice and the supply are acceptable, with advanced electronic signature and EDI named as examples rather than as mandatory methods. A model that assumes signatures are required overstates the requirement.

questions.text: By which method is authenticity of origin and integrity of content assured for this document, and is that method mandatory or elective in the governing jurisdiction?
answer_data: Assurance method (business controls, electronic signature or seal, EDI)
Statement of whether the method is legally required or elective

questions.text: What reliable audit trail links this invoice to the underlying supply, and which documents form it?
answer_data: Ordered set of linking documents (order, delivery, receipt, contract)
Description of the control that creates the link
Gaps in the trail and their justification
Actor responsible for maintaining the trail

questions.text: Where a signature or seal is applied, what exact byte scope does it cover and what does it leave unprotected?
answer_data: Elements or attachments outside the scope
Verification outcome with instant and verifying actor

questions.text: How is assurance maintained for the whole storage period as algorithms and certificates age?
answer_data: Long-term validation or archival timestamp strategy
Re-protection schedule and last execution instant
Fallback where re-protection was not performed

data_elements.name: Assurance method
data_elements.description: Declared method by which authenticity of origin and integrity of content are assured.

data_elements.name: Content digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest over the canonical byte form of the business document, with the algorithm identifier.

data_elements.name: Signature or seal record
data_elements.description: Signature or seal with signer or sealer reference, format, level, signing instant and covered scope.

data_elements.name: Audit trail link
data_elements.description: Typed link from the invoice to a document that forms part of the reliable audit trail to the supply.

artifacts.name: Integrity evidence set
artifacts.description: Bundle of digests, signature or seal records, timestamp tokens and verification outcomes for the document and its attachments, retained for the whole storage period.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus evidence sequence; each element content-addressed by its digest.

artifacts.name: Business control description
artifacts.description: Documented description of the business controls that create the reliable audit trail between the invoice and the supply, usable as evidence to an auditor where no signature is applied.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the control register identifier in the issuer's control system of record.

findings.name: Tax authority clearance, registration and reporting acknowledgement
findings.description: In continuous transaction control regimes the tax authority or its agent registers the invoice before or at the moment of issue and returns an identifier, an acknowledgement instant and often a signed code. That authority-side identifier is the master-system identifier for that jurisdiction and outranks the issuer's own number for legal purposes.

questions.text: Which clearance or reporting regime governs this document, and is registration a precondition of validity or a subsequent reporting duty?
answer_data: Applicability threshold that brought the document into scope

questions.text: What identifier, acknowledgement and signed code does the authority return, and how are they bound to the document?
answer_data: Acknowledgement reference and instant with explicit offset

questions.text: Within what deadline must registration occur, measured from which event?
answer_data: Deadline duration and its measurement basis

questions.text: What happens when clearance is rejected or unavailable, and what interim status may the document hold?
answer_data: Rejection reason returned by the authority
Permitted interim status and its limits

data_elements.name: Clearance identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier assigned by the tax authority or its agent upon registration of the document.

data_elements.name: Clearance acknowledgement instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the authority acknowledged registration, with explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Clearance token
data_elements.description: Signed code or machine-readable token returned by the authority and required to be carried on the document.

data_elements.name: Clearance status
data_elements.description: Outcome of the registration attempt, including rejection reasons where applicable.

artifacts.name: Clearance response record
artifacts.description: The authority's response as received: assigned identifier, acknowledgement reference and instant, signed token, status and any rejection reasons, retained as the evidence that the document was lawfully registered.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the authority-assigned identifier, which is treated as the master-system identifier for the governing jurisdiction.

layers.name: Regulatory conformance and validation evidence
layers.description: Which particulars the law requires, how jurisdictional variants change them, and what evidence proves the document was checked.

findings.name: Mandatory particulars and jurisdictional variants
findings.description: The governing law prescribes an exhaustive list of particulars a full invoice must show, with reduced sets for simplified invoices and additional wording for special regimes. National usage specifications further constrain or extend the core semantic model, and language and translation obligations may apply during storage. Conformance is therefore always jurisdiction-qualified.

questions.text: Which jurisdiction's particulars apply to this document, and what determines that jurisdiction?
answer_data: Governing jurisdiction and its determination basis
Threshold or condition that triggered the reduced set

questions.text: Which conditional particulars are triggered by this document's circumstances, such as exemption, reverse charge, margin scheme or self-billing?
answer_data: Required wording or code per condition

questions.text: Which national or sectoral usage specification applies on top of the core model, and what does it change?
answer_data: Restrictions and additions relative to the core

questions.text: In which language is the document issued, and what translation obligation applies for audit during the storage period?
answer_data: Party responsible for producing a translation
Deadline for supplying a translation on request

data_elements.name: Governing jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction whose invoicing rules govern this document, with the basis of that determination.

data_elements.name: Particulars profile
data_elements.description: Identifier of the applicable particulars set (full, simplified, special regime).

data_elements.name: Conditional requirement
data_elements.description: A requirement triggered by the document's circumstances, with its required wording or code.

data_elements.name: Document language
data_elements.description: Language in which the document is issued.

artifacts.name: Particulars requirement matrix
artifacts.description: Jurisdiction-by-condition matrix stating which particulars are mandatory, conditional or forbidden, mapped to the model's data elements and to the rule identifiers that test them.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by jurisdiction code plus particulars profile plus matrix version.

findings.name: Validation results and conformance evidence
findings.description: Conformance is demonstrated by executing versioned validation artefacts — schema checks plus business rule sets, including rules layered by a usage specification on top of the core rules — and retaining the outcome. Passing the core rule set does not imply passing a network's additional rules, so the rule set identity must be recorded with the result.

questions.text: Which rule sets and artefact versions were executed against this document, and which were not?
answer_data: Rule set identifiers and artefact versions
Rule sets deliberately not executed and why

questions.text: What was the outcome per rule, and how are fatal errors distinguished from warnings?
answer_data: Failed rule identifiers with located elements
Instant of execution with explicit offset

questions.text: How is a document revalidated when rule sets are updated on their release cycle, and what does an old pass result mean afterwards?
answer_data: Artefact release version at original validation
Revalidation policy and last revalidation outcome
Statement of the evidential value of a superseded pass

questions.text: What may a receiver do with a document that fails validation, and who decides?
answer_data: Permitted outcomes (reject, accept with exception, quarantine)

data_elements.name: Rule set identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of a validation rule set executed against the document.

data_elements.name: Rule outcome
data_elements.description: Per-rule result with severity and the located element.

data_elements.name: Validation instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which validation was executed, with explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Validation verdict
data_elements.description: Aggregate conformance determination for the executed rule sets.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: Retained report of a validation run: rule set identifiers and versions, per-rule outcomes with severities and locations, aggregate verdict, executing system and execution instant.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus rule set version plus run sequence number.

bundles.name: Exchange, retention and governance
bundles.description: How the document is serialised and routed, how long it must be kept and how it is disposed of, and who owns, may access and must be able to audit it.
bundles.rationale: Syntax binding, network routing, storage obligations and role-scoped access are the operating surface an agent must handle to move an invoice between organisations lawfully; storage obligations and the acceptability of storage location are set by law, while transport is set by network specifications.

layers.name: Serialisation, routing and delivery evidence
layers.description: How the same invoice semantics are carried across syntaxes and networks without loss, and what evidence exists that it arrived.

findings.name: Syntax binding and semantic fidelity across serialisations
findings.description: The same invoice semantics are bound to different syntaxes — a business-language XML document family, a cross-industry XML syntax, and hybrid carriers embedding one inside a rendition. Bindings are not bijective: extensions, code-list versions and structural differences make round-tripping lossy, so fidelity must be measured rather than assumed.

questions.text: Which syntax binding carries this instance, and which syntax versions and code-list versions does it depend on?
answer_data: Schema or schema module set referenced
Code list identifiers and versions bound
Profile level within the syntax where applicable

questions.text: What semantic loss occurs when this instance is transformed into another supported syntax?
Does the instance carry extension content beyond the core semantic model, and how must a receiver treat it?
Are all calculated values explicitly present rather than left for the receiver to infer?
answer_data: List of calculated values present in the instance
Any omitted value and its justification
Rule forbidding inference of omitted values

data_elements.name: Syntax identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the syntax binding used to serialise the instance.

data_elements.name: Code list binding
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of each code list the instance depends on.

data_elements.name: Extension content
data_elements.description: Content carried beyond the core semantic model, with its governing namespace.

data_elements.name: Transformation record
data_elements.description: Record of a syntax transformation with source, target, mapping version, losses and executing actor.

artifacts.name: Syntax mapping manifest
artifacts.description: Manifest binding each model data element to its location in every supported syntax, with the mapping version, unmappable elements and the round-trip fidelity result.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by source syntax identifier plus target syntax identifier plus mapping version.

findings.name: Routing identifiers, envelope and delivery evidence
findings.description: On a four-corner network the document is addressed by participant identifier, document type identifier and process identifier, discovered through service metadata, wrapped in a message envelope and transported under a defined profile. Transport-level receipt proves delivery to an access point, not business acceptance by the buyer — conflating the two is a common and consequential error.

questions.text: Which participant, document type and process identifiers address this transmission, and from which schemes are they drawn?
answer_data: Sender and receiver participant identifiers with scheme codes

questions.text: How was the receiver's capability and endpoint discovered, and what was the state of that lookup at send time?
answer_data: Capability match outcome for the document type
Instant of the lookup with explicit offset

questions.text: What envelope wraps the business document, and what does it assert that the document itself does not?
answer_data: Envelope header fields and their values
Relationship between envelope identifiers and document identifiers
Rule excluding the envelope from the business document digest

questions.text: What evidence exists that the document was delivered, and how is it distinguished from business acceptance?
answer_data: Explicit statement that receipt is not acceptance
Link to any separate business response

data_elements.name: Participant identifier
data_elements.description: Network address of a sender or receiver, with its scheme code.

data_elements.name: Document type identifier
data_elements.description: Network-level identifier of the document type and customization being exchanged.

data_elements.name: Envelope header
data_elements.description: Message envelope header carrying routing and typing metadata around the business document.

data_elements.name: Transport receipt
data_elements.description: Acknowledgement of delivery at transport level, with reference and instant.

artifacts.name: Transmission record
artifacts.description: Record of one transmission attempt: routing identifiers, discovery result, envelope headers, transport profile, outcome, receipt reference and instants, retained as delivery evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the envelope message identifier assigned by the sending access point, linked to the document authoritative identifier.

layers.name: Retention, storage and disposition
layers.description: How long the document and its evidence must be kept, where, in what condition, and how it is lawfully destroyed.

findings.name: Retention period, storage conditions, holds and erasure conflict
findings.description: Both issuer and recipient must retain invoices for a period fixed by national law, keeping authenticity, integrity and legibility intact and making them accessible to authorities on request; storage location and method are otherwise flexible. Retention interacts badly with personal-data erasure rights, and a legal hold must be able to suspend disposition without altering the record.

questions.text: What retention period applies to this document, from which trigger event is it measured, and which jurisdiction sets it?
answer_data: Trigger event and its date or instant

questions.text: What conditions must storage preserve for the whole period, and how is compliance monitored?
answer_data: Storage location and any cross-border constraint
Monitoring checks performed and their instants

questions.text: How is disposition suspended by a legal hold or dispute, and how is the suspension evidenced and lifted?
answer_data: Hold identifier, reason and placing authority
Documents and evidence within the hold scope
Rule that a hold never alters record content

questions.text: How is a personal-data erasure request reconciled with a statutory retention obligation on the same document?
answer_data: Personal data elements identified on the document
Legal basis asserted for continued retention
Restriction applied instead of erasure (access limitation, minimised projection)
Decision record with the deciding actor and instant

questions.text: What evidence is produced when disposition is finally executed?
answer_data: Execution instant with explicit offset and executing actor
Retained tombstone metadata and its scope

data_elements.name: Retention period
data_elements.description: Duration for which the document must be retained, with its measurement basis.

data_elements.name: Retention trigger event
data_elements.description: Event from which the retention period is measured.

data_elements.name: Storage location
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction and system in which the document and its evidence are stored.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: A suspension of disposition with reason, placing authority and placement and release instants.

data_elements.name: Disposition record
data_elements.description: Record of the executed disposition action with authorisation, actor and instant.

data_elements.name: Personal data marker
data_elements.description: Marks elements carrying personal data so that minimised projections and access restrictions can be applied.

artifacts.name: Retention schedule assignment
artifacts.description: Assignment of a retention class to the document with period, trigger, computed disposition date, storage constraints and any active holds.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus retention class identifier; schedule itself keyed by its registered class identifier.

artifacts.name: Disposition certificate
artifacts.description: Evidence artefact recording that a lawful disposition was executed, naming the authorisation, action, executing actor, instant and retained tombstone metadata.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus disposition sequence number; retained after the document itself is destroyed.

layers.name: Ownership, access projections and provenance
layers.description: Who owns the record, who may see which part of it, and how every handling act is traceable.

findings.name: Ownership, custodianship and role-scoped projections
findings.description: The issuing party owns the record; a service provider, access point or archiving provider may hold and process it as custodian without acquiring ownership. Different roles need different slices — a routing party needs envelope metadata only, an auditor needs the evidentiary set, a tax authority needs the full particulars — so projections are the access mechanism, not ad hoc field hiding.

questions.text: Who owns this record, who holds it as custodian, and what does the custodian agreement permit?
Which role-scoped projections exist, and which elements does each include and exclude?
On what basis may a tax or judicial authority obtain access, and what is the response obligation?
answer_data: Legal basis for the access request
Record of what was disclosed and to whom

questions.text: What secondary use of invoice content is permitted to a custodian, and what is prohibited?
answer_data: Consent or contractual basis where required

data_elements.name: Owning party
data_elements.description: Reference to the party that owns the record.

data_elements.name: Custodian party
data_elements.description: Reference to a party holding or processing the record on the owner's behalf, with its role.

data_elements.name: Projection definition
data_elements.description: Named role-scoped view listing included and excluded elements.

data_elements.name: Disclosure record
data_elements.description: Record of a disclosure to an authority or third party with basis, scope, recipient and instant.

artifacts.name: Access projection set
artifacts.description: Registered set of role-scoped projections over the document with their element inclusion and exclusion rules and approving authority, applied uniformly across every storage format and interface.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by projection identifier plus version; bound to the model identifier rather than to any single document.

findings.name: Provenance and end-to-end audit trail
findings.description: Every act on the document — generation, transformation, signing, clearance, transmission, validation, storage, disclosure, disposition — is recorded with the acting party, the acting system and an instant, distinguishing when the act happened from when it was observed. This is what allows an agent to answer for the document years later.

questions.text: Which parties and systems handled this document and in what order?
answer_data: Ordered handling chain with party and system references

questions.text: Which content was generated, derived or transformed rather than authored, and from what source?
How are event times separated from observation and ingestion times where the two differ?
answer_data: Event instant asserted by the acting system
Observation or ingestion instant recorded by the receiving system

questions.text: How would an unauthorised change to the audit trail itself be detected?
answer_data: Verification procedure and last verification instant

data_elements.name: Handling event
data_elements.description: A recorded act on the document with type, acting party, acting system and event instant.

data_elements.name: Observation instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which a handling act was observed or ingested, distinct from the event instant.

data_elements.name: Derivation source
data_elements.description: Reference to the input from which a derived value was produced, with the rule applied.

data_elements.name: Audit trail chain digest
data_elements.description: Digest chaining log entries so that removal or alteration of an entry is detectable.

artifacts.name: Provenance record
artifacts.description: Chained, append-only record of every handling act with actor, system, event instant, observation instant, inputs and outputs, verifiable independently of the document store.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by document authoritative identifier plus entry sequence number, with each entry carrying the digest of the previous entry.

functions.name: Issue commercial document
functions.description: Assemble and fix a billing document from commercial inputs, assign its identifier within the issuer's series, set the legally relevant dates and freeze content as immutable.
inputs: Commercial inputs (order, contract, fulfilment records, priced lines)
Party references for all required roles
outputs: Issued billing document with authoritative identifier
preconditions: Issuing authority established, including any self-billing or outsourcing mandate
Number series available and its sequence rule known
Required particulars for the governing jurisdiction determinable
effects: Document content becomes immutable; later change requires a new document
Statutory issue-deadline clock is assessed against the chargeable event
Retention trigger becomes computable

functions.name: Compute tax breakdown and totals
functions.description: Derive tax breakdown groups, document totals, rounding and amount due from lines, allowances and charges, stating every calculated value explicitly rather than leaving it to be inferred.
inputs: Invoice lines with tax category assignments
Applicable tax rates and exemption reasons
preconditions: Tax category and rate resolvable for every amount including allowances and charges
Currency and any tax accounting currency determined
effects: All calculated values are present in the instance
Arithmetic rule set becomes checkable by any receiver

functions.name: Validate against declared specification
functions.description: Execute schema and business rule artefacts for the declared specification, including any rules a network layers on the core rule set, and retain the outcome as conformance evidence.
inputs: Document instance in a supported syntax
outputs: Validation report with per-rule outcomes and severities
List of rule sets deliberately not executed
preconditions: Artefact version resolvable from the registry
Syntax binding recognised
effects: Conformance claim becomes evidenced rather than asserted
Failing documents are routed to the exception path rather than transmitted

functions.name: Register or clear with tax authority
functions.description: Submit the document to a clearance or reporting authority where the jurisdiction requires it, capture the returned identifier, acknowledgement and token, and bind them to the document digest.
preconditions: Regime applicability determined for the jurisdiction and document type
Document conforms to the regime's required content
effects: Authority-assigned identifier becomes the master-system identifier for that jurisdiction
Lawful delivery to the buyer becomes permitted where clearance is a precondition

functions.name: Transmit and route document
functions.description: Discover the receiver's capability and endpoint, wrap the document in the network envelope, transmit under the agreed transport profile and retain delivery evidence.
outputs: Transmission record with routing identifiers and outcome
Failure reason where delivery did not succeed
preconditions: Receiver capability for the document type confirmed by metadata lookup
Transport profile and security requirements satisfied
effects: Delivery evidence exists, distinct from business acceptance
Retry or fallback path is triggered on failure

functions.name: Verify authenticity and integrity
functions.description: Confirm that the document originates from the asserted issuer and that its content is unaltered, using the declared assurance method — business controls, signature or seal, or exchange controls — and record the outcome.
inputs: Document instance and its recorded digest
Declared assurance method and any signature or token
Audit trail links to the underlying supply
outputs: Verification outcome with verifying actor and instant
preconditions: Digest recorded at ingestion is available
Assurance method and its parameters are known
effects: A verified document may be relied on as evidence
A mismatch quarantines the artefact and blocks disposition

functions.name: Match to order and receipt
functions.description: Reconcile the document and its lines against referenced order and goods receipt records within declared tolerances to support an acceptance decision.
outputs: Matching result record with per-line outcomes
preconditions: References resolvable to accessible records
Matching mode selected (two-way, three-way, line-level)
effects: Acceptance or rejection decision becomes evidenced
Unresolvable references are escalated rather than silently ignored

functions.name: Record buyer response
functions.description: Capture the receiver's business response — acknowledgement, acceptance, conditional acceptance, rejection or dispute — with coded reasons and the authorising role.
preconditions: Responder authorised within their limits
Response window still open where one applies
effects: Business acceptance is recorded separately from transport receipt
A dispute suspends practical payment expectation without altering the document

functions.name: Issue correction or credit
functions.description: Amend an issued document by producing a new document that refers specifically and unambiguously to it, using the mechanism lawful in the governing jurisdiction.
inputs: Original document identifier and issue date
outputs: New billing document with preceding-document reference
preconditions: Original document retrievable and its digest recorded
Chosen mechanism lawful for the document type and jurisdiction
effects: The original remains unmodified and retrievable
The commercial claim is changed only through the chain, never by editing

functions.name: Render human-readable form
functions.description: Produce or verify the human-readable representation of the document, including hybrid carriers, and confirm that it agrees with the structured representation and remains legible.
preconditions: Required particulars available for display
Preservation profile supported by the rendering toolchain
effects: Legibility obligation for the storage period becomes demonstrable
Divergence between visual and structured forms is detected rather than latent

functions.name: Apply retention and disposition
functions.description: Assign the retention class, compute the earliest disposition date, honour holds and, when eligible, execute disposition with evidence.
inputs: Active legal holds and dispute states
preconditions: Retention period and trigger determined for the governing jurisdiction
No active hold or unresolved dispute in scope
effects: Records are not destroyed while under hold or dispute
Disposition leaves auditable tombstone evidence after the record is gone

functions.name: Project role-scoped view
functions.description: Produce the projection appropriate to a requesting role — routing metadata, evidentiary set, authority disclosure, minimised personal-data view — and record the disclosure.
inputs: Requesting role and legal or contractual basis
outputs: Disclosure record with recipient, scope and instant
Denial reason where the request is refused
preconditions: Projection registered and approved
Requester authenticated and their basis established
effects: Access is granted by projection rather than by ad hoc field hiding
Every disclosure is auditable and attributable

functions.name: Issue self-billed invoice
functions.description: Allow the customer, under agreement, to issue an invoice in the supplier's name, including the Self-billing mention, and capture supplier acceptance or dispute.
outputs: supplier acceptance status or dispute notice
preconditions: a self-billing agreement authorises the customer to issue in the supplier's name
effects: the issuer role is inverted to the customer while the supply stays the supplier's
supplier reconciliation outcome is captured, including a self-billing credit note where needed

functions.name: Present payment claim
functions.description: Expose payable amount, due date or terms, payment means and payee so a payment process can settle the invoice without storing the payment here.

payment means and payee financial account

either a payment due date or payment terms is present
